description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §11.4 'Initial conditions (the `ic` op)' at rank ZERO: an `ic`-LHS equation is the initial value of its target, a 0-D component's `ic` RHS is a scalar, a state with no `ic` falls back to its declared `default`, and a test's `initial_conditions` overrides the `ic` for that run. Model PARAMETERS bind in an `ic` RHS's build-time evaluation scope (§6.6.5), keyed by LOCAL parameter name (§6.6). Every state of `scalar_ic.esm` declares a `default` that DIFFERS from its `ic`, so a binding that drops the equation reads the default and is caught rather than masked; `y` integrates `D(y)/dt = u` so the seeded value also has to reach the trajectory. `scalar_ic_in_array_model.esm` re-runs the same contract for a 0-D state that shares a model with an ARRAY state, which routes the document through each binding's ARRAY runtime instead of its scalar one. Before this category, Python dropped every 0-D `ic` on BOTH pathways (the scalar-SymPy one lowers only `D(x)/dt` and algebraic equations; the array-NumPy one folded only array-shaped targets and no-op'd the rest) and Rust dropped it on its scalar interpreter (`ic` matched neither `state_lhs_name` nor `observed_lhs_name` in `classify_equations`). Both were SILENT: `ic(u) ~ 3.0` ran from the default and the inline test still reported a verdict. Julia folded both ranks correctly and is the reference binding: its `run_pde_tests` minted both goldens.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator / inline test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator / inline test runner

assertions.note: ic(u) = 3.0, a plain literal; the declared default is 0.0
ic(w) = 2*A with A at its declared 2.0 (§6.6.5)
no ic equation: the declared default stands
non-vacuity: y(1) = integral of the ic-seeded u
parameter_overrides {A: 10} reaches the ic's build-time scope
parameter-free ic unmoved by the override
parameter-free trajectory unmoved by the override
§11.4 run-time override beats the ic equation
the overridden u reaches the trajectory
a state the run override does not name keeps its ic
array ic broadcast: the anchor proving the array path is intact
0-D ic inside the ARRAY runtime: 2*B with B at its declared 3.0
parameter_overrides {B: 10} reaches the 0-D ic in the array runtime
